TEXT A · PRESENT SIMPLE · Their Routine

David manages a small team, and Tom is the newest member. Their routine runs on one simple rule: everyone follows the process. Every Monday, David has his assistant prepare the weekly report, it's just part of the job, nothing personal. He doesn't let deadlines slide, but he does let the team choose their own tools, as long as the numbers are right in the end.

When something looks off, David makes Tom double-check it before it goes out. Tom, for his part, sometimes gets David to explain things twice when he doesn't fully understand, and David doesn't mind that at all. Company policy doesn't allow employees to submit unreviewed drafts, and David takes that rule seriously. He lets junior staff make small mistakes, that's how people learn, but he never lets the same mistake happen twice.

TEXT B · PAST SIMPLE · Last Week

Last week didn't go the way it usually does. Tom got David to accept a rushed draft without a full review, David was in a hurry that morning and agreed. It backfired almost immediately. The report had errors, and David made Tom redo the whole thing before 5pm, no exceptions this time. David didn't let it slide the way he sometimes does.

Instead, David had Tom go through every line out loud, one by one, at his desk. Tom didn't get David to change his mind, not this time, no matter how he explained it. By Friday, the report was finally done, and David let the whole team leave early, everyone had earned it.

TEXT C · CONTINUOUS & WOULD · This Week

This week, things are different. David is having the team double-check every report before it goes to a client, it's the new normal for now, not a punishment. Tom is getting better at catching his own mistakes, David has noticed the change. David isn't making anyone stay late this week, the team earned some trust back.

David is allowing Tom to review his own drafts before sending them over, a small change, but a real one. Tom would rather have more independence, and David is slowly starting to agree with him. Next month, if this week goes well, David is planning to let Tom lead the report entirely on his own.
